quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Your flatmate asked if you can swap bin duty this week. Subject: Re: Bin duty swap / Greeting: Hey Cass, / Reply in a relaxed, friendly tone. Arrange the body and sign-off.
options: I'm off to my parents' on Friday, so I'll take it out before I leave.
You can owe me a coffee!
No worries, I can do it this week.

Cheers,
Marek
quests.hint: Casual tone: short sentences, contractions, a joke. What sequence keeps it easy and light?
quests.explanation: In a casual email, the answer comes first and the details follow. The joke at the end fits the tone with a flatmate, but would sound out of place if sent to a manager.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are inviting your team-mates to a surprise party for the coach. Lay out the message.
options: Hi all,

Thanks, and see you there!
Maya
We're throwing Coach a surprise party after Saturday's game, at the clubhouse from 5:30. Don't say a word to her, and bring a snack if you can!
Subject: Shhh! Surprise for Coach Dee
quests.hint: Excitement can show in the wording, but the essential details should still be easy to find.
quests.explanation: A friendly tone allows exclamation marks and jokes, but readers still need time, place and what to bring. The warning ('Don't say a word') is placed after the plan so people read the plan first.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You've just finished a group project and want to thank your group in the chat email. Arrange it.
options: Hi everyone,

Cheers,
Joshua
Subject: We did it!
Thanks so much for all your hard work on the presentation. I think we nailed it, and I'm buying pizza on Friday to celebrate.
quests.hint: Celebrations in friendly emails are best when a plan follows the thanks.
quests.explanation: The informal words ('nailed it', 'Cheers') are correct here because the readers are peers. Adding a concrete plan (pizza on Friday) turns appreciation into an action.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You're asking a local bike shop when your repair will be ready. Set out the email in a neutral tone.
options: Hello,
Subject: Bike repair for Ruth Malik: pick-up date
I left my bike with you on Monday to have the brakes replaced. Could you tell me when it will be ready to collect?

Thank you,
Ruth Malik
quests.hint: Neutral is neither chatty nor stiff. Pick the simplest greeting and sign-off.
quests.explanation: Neutral emails avoid both slang and heavy formality. 'Hello' and 'Thank you' are safe with most service businesses, and the writer's name in the subject helps the shop find the job.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Question about the club's Wednesday session / Greeting: Hi Claire, / You barely know Claire, the club secretary. Arrange the body in a neutral tone.
options: I joined the running club last month.
I just want to be sure before I come.

Thanks,
Noel
Are Wednesday sessions still starting at 6:30 pm now that the clocks have changed?
quests.hint: With someone you barely know, be friendly but plain. Answer 'what would they need to know first?'
quests.explanation: Notice the sequence: context, question, reason. A neutral request explains itself briefly without over-apologising or chatting.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You want to tell a tutor you no longer need lessons. Build the email.
options: I have decided to stop lessons at the end of this month, as my exams are approaching. Thank you for everything you have taught me.
Dear Mr Iyer,
Subject: Ending my piano lessons

Best wishes,
Charlotte Yeo
quests.hint: Even a neutral message that ends a service should show appreciation.
quests.explanation: The decision is stated clearly, followed by the reason and thanks. Ending on appreciation keeps the tone courteous without turning it into a long farewell.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are writing to your line manager of two years about a change to your working hours. Put together the semi-formal email.
options: Hi Hilary,
I would like to ask whether I could start at 8 am and finish at 4 pm, as my childcare arrangements have changed. I can begin from next month, or whenever suits the team.

Kind regards,
Walter Okon
Subject: Request to change my start time
quests.hint: You know each other well. First names are fine but the request still needs a polite structure.
quests.explanation: Semi-formal is the everyday tone of most offices: first names, but polite requests and a professional sign-off. The flexible timing at the end shows you're considering the team.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A student is asking a university tutor for a recommendation. Assemble the email.
options: Subject: Reference for my Master's application

Best wishes,
Daisy Chan
Dear Dr Menon,
You taught me in two modules last year, and I am now applying for a Master's programme at Leeds. Would you be willing to write me a reference? The deadline is 15 December.
quests.hint: Remind the tutor who you are before asking. Then give the deadline.
quests.explanation: Asking 'Would you be willing' allows the tutor to decline without embarrassment, which is good for both sides. A clear deadline lets him plan.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are writing to your child's football coach about a change in pick-up. Subject: Pick-up on Saturday / Greeting: Hello Coach Adaeze, / Arrange the body.
options: Please let me know if the club needs anything else from me.

Kind regards,
Sheila Okoro
She'll be in a grey Toyota, and she'll wait by the main gate.
My mother will collect Tobi after Saturday's match instead of me.
quests.hint: Practical details come before the offer of further help.
quests.explanation: Coaches want to know who will collect the child and how to recognise them. Semi-formal wording keeps things polite without adding unnecessary formality.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are writing to a government office to report a change of address. Piece together the formal email.
options: I am writing to inform you that I moved to 23 Beech Avenue, Nottingham, NG3 5AB, on 1 March. Please update your records and confirm by email.
Subject: Notification of change of address, ref. NI 442 190 K
Dear Sir or Madam,

Yours faithfully,
Esther Kamara
quests.hint: In a formal email, the purpose is stated directly with no chatting.
quests.explanation: Formal emails use full sentences, no contractions and a specific request. The reference number in the subject helps a large organisation route the message.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A resident writes to the town council objecting to a planned building. Set out the email.
options:
Yours faithfully,
Mr R. Kingsley
I am writing to object to planning application 24/00871 for a four-storey building on Cross Street. I believe it would reduce light to nearby homes and increase traffic on an already busy road.
Subject: Objection to planning application 24/00871
Dear Planning Officer,
quests.hint: Formal objections state the position first and then give reasons. Do not begin with anger.
quests.explanation: Officials need the application reference and your position first. Reasons should be brief and objective, because a calm tone is more persuasive than an emotional one.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are writing to a judge's clerk to ask whether a court date can be moved. Structure the email.
options: I am due to attend a hearing on 9 May, but I will be in hospital for a scheduled operation. I would be grateful if the hearing could be rearranged, and I can provide a medical letter.
Dear Clerk of the Court,

Yours faithfully,
Cornelius Bright
Subject: Request to rearrange hearing on 9 May, case 2023/771
quests.hint: The register is at its most formal here. Check that the request is respectful and complete.
quests.explanation: In legal and official contexts, precise references and respectful wording matter. The offer of a medical letter shows you take the process seriously.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A client has renewed their contract, and you'd like to thank them warmly but professionally. Arrange the email.
options: Dear Ms Hartley,
Subject: Thank you for renewing with us

Warm regards,
Amit Desai
Thank you for renewing your contract for another year. We have enjoyed working with your team, and we look forward to supporting your plans for the new season.
quests.hint: Warm professional means genuine appreciation without becoming casual.
quests.explanation: 'Warm regards' and personal language ('we have enjoyed working with your team') build a relationship, while the structure stays professional. This is the tone of many client-facing roles.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are welcoming a new supplier to your company's network. Subject: Welcome to Harbourline / Greeting: Dear Mr Sokolov, / Arrange the body and sign-off.
options:
Kind regards,
Rosalind Fyfe
Your first order will arrive on Monday, and Lucy Grant in Purchasing will be your contact.
Please tell us if there is anything we can do to make things easier for you.
We are pleased to welcome Sokolov Packaging to our supplier network.
quests.hint: Welcome, practical information, then an open offer of help.
quests.explanation: A warm welcome first makes the practical information feel friendly. The closing offer shows that you care about the relationship, not only the transaction.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are apologising to a long-standing client for a late delivery. Subject: Your delivery on 6 June / Greeting: Dear Mrs Delgado, / Arrange the warm but professional body.
options: I am sorry that your order arrived two days late, and I understand how this affected your event.
We have refunded the delivery charge, and I will make sure future orders are prioritised.
The delay was caused by a problem at our warehouse.

Yours sincerely,
Marcus Ellery
quests.hint: Warm professionals show understanding first, then explain, then compensate.
quests.explanation: Expressing understanding of the client's situation before explaining the cause shows empathy. The compensation then comes as a solution, not as a defence.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You need a colleague to reply to an email you sent last week. Lay out the message so the request does not sound like a complaint.
options:
Thanks,
Pablo
Subject: Quick check on the venue email
Hi Lauren,
I know you've had a busy week, so I wanted to check that my email about the venue reached you. Could you let me know your thoughts by Friday?
quests.hint: Acknowledging the reader's situation before the request softens the tone.
quests.explanation: Starting with understanding ('I know you've had a busy week') prepares the reader for the request. It sounds much gentler than 'You haven't replied'.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You want a supplier to send a delayed invoice. Subject: Invoice for May / Greeting: Dear Mr Patel, / Arrange the body and sign-off.
options: I have not yet received the invoice for May, and I would like to include it in this month's payment run.

Kind regards,
Susan Whyte
Would you be able to send it by Thursday?
I hope you are well.
quests.hint: Cushion the request with a friendly opening, then explain, then ask.
quests.explanation: 'I hope you are well' is a small courtesy that makes the direct request feel less abrupt. Explaining why you need the invoice helps the supplier prioritise.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A student wants a teacher to reconsider a deadline. Set out the email.
options: Thank you for explaining the project so clearly. I wonder whether it would be possible to have until Monday, as I have two other deadlines this week?
Dear Mr Hobbs,
Subject: Question about the project deadline

Best wishes,
Isla Brennan
quests.hint: Begin with appreciation and ask using tentative language.
quests.explanation: Appreciation before a request shows goodwill. 'I wonder whether it would be possible' is a tentative, respectful way to ask for something the teacher might refuse.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Your company has to decline a customer's application for credit. Structure the letter so that the news is clear but kind.
options: Dear Mr Amoah,
Subject: Your credit application, ref. CR-7701

Thank you for applying for a Harbourline credit account. After reviewing your application, we are unable to offer credit at this time, but you are welcome to apply again after six months. Please contact us if you would like to discuss the decision.

Yours sincerely,
Anne-Marie Lloyd
quests.hint: Bad news should be clear but not abrupt. What comes before it and after it?
quests.explanation: Starting with thanks acknowledges the effort, then the decision is stated plainly. Offering a next step (reapply) leaves the reader with something constructive.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You must tell a team member that the office move is delayed. Subject: Update on the office move / Greeting: Hi all, / Arrange the body.
options: In the meantime, everything stays as it is, and I'll send you a packing schedule next week.

Thanks for your patience,
Lindiwe
The building works have overrun, so we will now move on 14 July instead of 30 June.
I'm afraid I have some disappointing news about the move.
quests.hint: A warning sentence, the fact, then the practical impact.
quests.explanation: A soft opening ('I'm afraid') prepares the reader. The fact follows without excuses, and reassurance about what happens next reduces anxiety.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are turning down a friend's request to borrow money. Arrange the reply.
options: Thank you for trusting me with this. I'm sorry, but I can't lend money at the moment, and I don't want to say yes and then let you down.
Subject: Re: Can you help me out?

Take care,
Helen
Hi Toby,
quests.hint: A refusal to a friend needs honesty and care. Which order shows both?
quests.explanation: Thanking him first respects his trust. Giving a clear, kind 'no' avoids false hope, and the reason focuses on not letting him down rather than on his request.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are thrilled about being offered a place on a course. Assemble the reply to the admissions tutor.
options: Subject: Re: Offer of a place on the MA in Journalism

Yours sincerely,
Beth Ashworth
Dear Professor Ito,
Thank you very much for the offer of a place on the MA in Journalism. I am delighted to accept, and I look forward to starting in September.
quests.hint: Enthusiasm can be sincere without being excessive. Match it to the register.
quests.explanation: 'Delighted' expresses enthusiasm in formal language. Over-excited phrases like 'I'm SO happy!!!' would be out of place with an admissions tutor.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A friend has helped you prepare for an interview, and you got the job! Arrange the email.
options: Hi Chidi,
Your mock interview questions were exactly what they asked, and I've just been offered the job. I can't thank you enough, so dinner is definitely on me!
Subject: I got the job!!

Love,
Adaeze
quests.hint: Informal writing can be exclamatory. Give the news, credit, then the gesture.
quests.explanation: Between close friends, extra punctuation and warmth feel natural. Crediting the friend's help and offering dinner shows real appreciation.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are thanking a mentor for a year of guidance. Piece together the email.
options: Subject: Thank you for a great year
Dear Ms Alvarez,

With best wishes,
Jonah Ellis
Over the past year, your advice on presentation skills and career choices has made a real difference to my confidence. I am very grateful for your time and patience.
quests.hint: Sincere appreciation is specific. What did she actually help with?
quests.explanation: Specific examples (presentation skills, career choices) make thanks credible. The tone is warm but measured, which suits a mentor relationship.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A tenant asks the landlord to repair a broken boiler for the third time. Arrange the email; be clear and firm but not rude.
options: I have reported the broken boiler on 4 and 11 November, and it has still not been repaired. I would be grateful if you could arrange a repair by Friday, as we have been without heating for two weeks.

Yours sincerely,
Sofia Marin
Subject: Boiler repair: third request, flat 3, 12 Park Road
Dear Mr Hendricks,
quests.hint: A firm email needs facts, dates and a deadline, but polite wording.
quests.explanation: Firmness comes from facts (dates, duration) and a deadline, not from angry language. 'I would be grateful' keeps the tone respectful even when your patience is running out.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are reminding your colleague of an agreed deadline. Subject: Reminder: figures due Thursday / Greeting: Hi Leo, / Arrange the body.
options: Could you confirm today that they will be ready?
The board pack goes out on Friday morning, so I can't wait any later.

Thanks,
Eva
Just a reminder that we agreed the sales figures would be ready by Thursday.
quests.hint: State the agreement, the reason for firmness, then request confirmation.
quests.explanation: Referring to the agreement ('we agreed') is more effective than blame. The Friday deadline explains why the timing matters.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A customer wants a refund and the company must say no to one part. Build the reply.
options: We have refunded the faulty blender in full, and the money will reach your account within five days. However, we are unable to refund the delivery charge, because this is not covered by our refund policy.
Subject: Your refund request, order 90211
Dear Ms Quinn,

Yours sincerely,
Katrin Lund
quests.hint: Positive news first, then the limit. Which order makes the refusal feel fair?
quests.explanation: Leading with what you can do makes the refusal easier to accept. The reason is stated once, briefly, and doesn't sound defensive.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You will be late to a meeting. Write to a close friend who is waiting in a café.
options:
See you soon,
Ria
Sorry, my train got held up! I'll be there by 12:45. Order me a coffee if you get there first.
Subject: Running 15 minutes late
Hey Sam,
quests.hint: Read the audience: close friend. Which sequence sounds like a quick message?
quests.explanation: This question begins a mini-lesson about audience. With a close friend, you can use exclamations and a small request. The same news to a client would sound different.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You will be late to a meeting. Write to a client who is waiting.
options: Dear Mr Nakamura,
Subject: Delay to our 12 pm meeting

Kind regards,
Ria Bhatt
I apologise, but my train has been delayed, and I will arrive at approximately 12:45. If you prefer, I am happy to start by phone or reschedule.
quests.hint: Now the reader is a client. What should you offer besides an apology?
quests.explanation: For a client, the apology is more formal, and you offer alternatives because their time is valuable. The core information (delay and new time) is the same, but the tone and options differ.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You will be late to a meeting. Write to your manager, who chairs the meeting.
options: Hi Diane,

Thanks,
Ria
My train has been delayed, and I expect to arrive by 12:45. I have sent the slides to Tom so he can begin the first item without me.
Subject: Running late for the 12 pm meeting
quests.hint: A manager cares about the plan, not just the apology. Which sequence shows you have taken care of it?
quests.explanation: For a manager, you keep it short, and you show you have limited the impact by handing over the slides. The warm-professional tone sits between the friend's message and the client's.
